_comment: Copy this file to config.json and fill in your details. Run `node setup.js` to be guided interactively.

person._country_note: 2-letter country code. US (default), CA, GB, AU, etc. Non-US users: 'state' holds province/region; 'zip' holds postal code (any format, e.g. K1A 0A6 or SW1A 1AA); 'phoneFormatted' is the raw phone number with no US formatting.
person._state_note: For non-US: province or region (e.g. ON for Ontario, NSW for New South Wales)
person._zip_note: For non-US: postal code in your country's format (e.g. K1A 0A6, SW1A 1AA, 2000)
person._phone_note: For non-US: phoneFormatted equals phone with no reformatting applied

capsolver._comment: Sign up free at capsolver.com - pay-as-you-go, costs pennies/month for this use case

captcha._comment: Solving CAPTCHAs yourself. Without a CapSolver key (or when CapSolver fails) a CAPTCHA broker used to fail on the spot; now the browser window comes to the front, your terminal beeps, you get a desktop notification, and the tool waits while you solve it, then submits the form for you. A broker nobody solved is logged as captcha_failed; run `aidr captchas` to retry only those, headed.
captcha._manual_comment: "auto" (default): wait for you only when the browser is visible AND you are at an interactive terminal (a scheduled run or Docker never waits). true: wait whenever the browser is visible, even without a terminal. false: never wait. A headless browser never waits whatever this says; run `aidr captchas` on a desktop machine instead.
captcha._manualTimeoutSec_comment: How long to wait for you on each CAPTCHA before moving on, in seconds (default 180, maximum 3600).

hibp._comment: Optional. Have I Been Pwned breach check (node watcher.js --breach-check). Get a key at https://haveibeenpwned.com/API/Key. Leave apiKey blank to disable.

accounts._comment: For sites that require a login. Leave password blank - setup.js will prompt you to create the account once, then store credentials here.

notify._comment: iMessage number to text results to (macOS only). Leave blank to disable.
notify._webhook_comment: Optional webhook URL for notifications on any OS (ntfy.sh, Slack, Discord). Leave blank to disable.

email._comment: SMTP config for sending opt-out emails. Required - without this, email brokers are logged as 'manual'. Gmail: host=smtp.gmail.com, port=587, use an App Password (myaccount.google.com/apppasswords). Outlook/Office365: host=smtp-mail.outlook.com, port=587.

smtp._ca_comment: Optional: path to a PEM certificate to trust for this server, for local bridges with a self-signed cert. Proton Mail Bridge: host=127.0.0.1, port=1025, export the cert from Bridge settings (Export TLS certificates) and set ca to its path, e.g. cert.pem.
smtp._allowInsecure_comment: Optional escape hatch, leave false. On every port except 465 the connection MUST upgrade with STARTTLS or the send fails; otherwise someone on the network can strip STARTTLS and read your SMTP password and the opt-out emails. Set true ONLY for a local relay on 127.0.0.1 that genuinely speaks plaintext.

relay._comment: OPTIONAL masked-email relay. When set, opt-out submissions use a per-person alias instead of person.email so brokers never get your real address. Currently supports provider 'simplelogin' via API. Apple Hide My Email and Firefox Relay are manual-only - see docs/relay.md. Omit this block entirely to submit with your real email (default). The relay FAILS CLOSED: if an alias cannot be created for a person, nothing is submitted for that person (and the run exits 1) rather than falling back to your real address. Add "failOpen": true to this block to allow that fallback, with a warning. With a relay set, email.smtp.from must be a dedicated sending address, not one of your real addresses: the From header is not masked, so a real sender would still reach every email broker (the run refuses those emails, and `aidr config check` warns).

retention._comment: OPTIONAL. Run logs, audit reports, form screenshots and monthly report PDFs hold your name and the list of brokers that have your data, and they pile up. Add "days": 180 here (a number of days, or text like "6m" or "1y"; at least 7 days) to delete the ones older than that at the end of each successful run. With no "days" key, everything is kept forever (the default). Never deleted, whatever you set: the newest run log and its journal, the newest audit report, complaints, state and config. `aidr purge --older-than 180d --dry-run` shows what an age would delete without deleting anything.

browser._comment: OPTIONAL browser settings; every field can stay blank. Each person in config gets their own browser profile folder under profileDir (named person-<n>-<hash>, never the person's name), so cookies and logins never carry from one person to the next. An existing single-person install keeps its current profile for the first person. Headless runs send a regular Chrome user agent instead of HeadlessChrome (same Chrome version); set userAgent below only to override that.

proxy._comment: OPTIONAL. Send every browser request through a proxy so brokers see its address, not yours. Leave server blank for none. server must start with http://, https:// or socks5:// and must not contain a username or password: put those in username and password (a secret, like email.smtp.pass). Chromium cannot log in to a socks5 proxy, so use http:// or https:// when your proxy needs credentials. bypass is an optional comma-separated list of hosts that skip the proxy, e.g. *.internal.example,localhost. A mistyped proxy stops the run; it never quietly falls back to your own connection.

browser._userAgent_comment: OPTIONAL. A full user agent string used as given, headless or not. Blank (default) means: the browser's own in headed runs, a regular Chrome string in headless runs.
